item.title: A Binary-Encoded Contraction T-Matrix Method for Acoustically Assisted Electromagnetic Inverse Scattering Imaging
item.description: Electromagnetic inverse scattering imaging (EISI) inherently suffers from strong nonlinearity and ill-posedness, particularly for high-contrast scatterers. These limitations can be mitigated through acoustically assisted electromagnetic inversion. In this work, a novel binary-encoded contraction T-matrix method (CT-MM) is proposed for acoustically assisted EISI. First, the scattering behaviors of electromagnetic and acoustic waves are jointly modeled within a unified T-matrix framework. Furthermore, a contraction scheme is introduced in the electromagnetic and acoustic formulations, which reduces the nonlinearity of the inversion model and provides a potentially exploitable encoding scheme. Second, by appropriately tuning the control factor in the contraction mapping, a binary-encoded method for the acoustic spatial support is proposed, i.e., zero for background and one for scatterers. Consequently, acoustic inversion is recast as the recovery of simple encoded values rather than the estimation of unknown acoustic properties (i.e., compressibility and density), although they are fully embedded within the proposed CT-MM. This is substantially different from existing methods. Finally, two new acoustically assisted electromagnetic inversion frameworks are developed, which exploit the acoustic-encoded reconstructions to guide and regularize electromagnetic imaging, thereby significantly alleviating the nonlinearity and ill-posedness of EISI. Representative imaging results are provided to validate the effectiveness, accuracy, and robustness of the proposed method. A comparison with other advanced joint inversion methods further highlights the advantages of the proposed method.
item.authors: Xinhui Zhang;Xiuzhu Ye;

item.title: VFM-Loc: Training-Free Cross-View Geo-Localization via Aligning Discriminative Visual Hierarchies
item.description: Cross-view geo-localization (CVGL) in remote sensing (RS) aims to locate a drone-view query by matching it to geo-tagged satellite images. Although supervised methods have achieved strong results on close-set benchmarks, they often fail to generalize to unconstrained, real-world scenarios due to severe viewpoint differences and dataset bias. To overcome these limitations, we present VFM-Loc, a training-free CVGL framework that leverages the generalizable visual representations from vision foundation models (VFMs). VFM-Loc identifies and matches discriminative visual clues across different viewpoints through a progressive alignment strategy. First, we design a hierarchical clue extraction mechanism using generalized mean (GeM) pooling and scale-weighted R-MAC to preserve distinctive visual clues across scales while maintaining hierarchical confidence. Second, we introduce a statistical manifold alignment pipeline based on domainwise principal component analysis (PCA) and orthogonal Procrustes (OPs) analysis, linearly aligning heterogeneous feature distributions in a shared metric space. Experiments demonstrate that VFM-Loc exhibits high accuracy on standard benchmarks and surpasses supervised methods by over 20% in recall@1 on the challenging large-oblique UAV–satellite cross-view (LO-UCV) dataset with large oblique angles. This work highlights that principled alignment of pretrained features can effectively bridge the cross-view gap, establishing a robust and training-free paradigm for real-world CVGL. The relevant code is made available at github.com/DingLei14/VFM-Loc
item.authors: Jun Lu;Zehao Sang;Haoqi Wei;Xiangyun Liu;Kun Zhu;Haitao Guo;Zhihui Gong;Lei Ding;

item.title: SA-ISAR Autofocusing and Cross-Range Scaling via Cross-Term-Aware Centroid Frequency–Chirp Rate Distribution Reconstruction
item.description: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) provides an effective means for noncooperative target observation through high-resolution imaging; nevertheless, sparse aperture ISAR (SA-ISAR) autofocusing and cross-range scaling (CRS) for targets with spatial-variant Doppler remain challenging because incomplete observations and spatial-variant phase errors (SVPEs) jointly degrade coherent integration. After translational motion compensation (TMC), this article exploits the centroid frequency–chirp rate (CFCR)-domain sparsity of the range-cell slow-time observations, which are characterized by a nonuniformly sampled multicomponent linear frequency-modulated (MCLFM) model. Accordingly, SA-ISAR autofocusing and CRS are cast as a CFCR-domain sparse reconstruction problem, for which this article proposes a Bayesian-covariance-aided pairwise-coupled Wiener reconstruction method for CFCR auto-terms, termed BPCW-ATR. A CFCR-domain sparse observation model based on instantaneous autocorrelation function (IAF) samples is first established, in which the desired auto-terms are linearized with respect to sparse CFCR-domain coefficients. In the proposed cross-term-aware Wiener framework, deterministic signal–signal cross-terms are parameterized by retained unordered CFCR-node pairs and incorporated into the observation covariance as structured interference, whereas the IAF-induced signal–noise cross-term and noise auto-term are modeled as stochastic disturbances whose covariance is adaptively inferred. Furthermore, to enable efficient CFCR-domain reconstruction, a structured 2-D preconditioned conjugate gradient (2D-PCG) solver is developed. The reconstructed CFCR auto-terms are then used for focused ISAR image formation, effective rotational velocity (ERV) estimation, and CRS. Experiments on simulated and measured data demonstrate that BPCW-ATR enables reliable CFCR-domain reconstruction and achieves robust SA-ISAR autofocusing and CRS under high missing rates (MRs) and low signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs).
item.authors: Qian Liu;Yuanyuan Wang;Juan Zhang;Fengzhou Dai;Yong Wang;

item.title: Domain-Consistent Pansharpening via Learnable Degradation Modeling and Amplitude–Phase Modulation
item.description: Deep learning (DL)-based pansharpening methods have achieved promising results under Wald’s protocol. However, their effectiveness on real satellite imagery is constrained by discrepancies between simulated degradation and real observations. Moreover, existing frequency-domain fusion methods insufficiently exploit the distinct yet complementary roles of amplitude and phase information. To address these issues, we propose a novel domain-consistent pansharpening framework via learnable degradation modeling and amplitude–phase modulation (DC-APM). First, separate degradation networks are trained for multispectral (MS) and panchromatic (PAN) images to generate data-adaptive training samples through reconstruction-constrained local distribution alignment, reducing reliance on predefined degradation assumptions. Second, we design an amplitude–phase modulation network (APM-Net) for feature fusion. An amplitude–phase modulation module (APMM) enhances spectral and structural representations through explicit amplitude–phase decomposition, while a lightweight cross-domain interaction unit (CIU) enables bidirectional information exchange for adaptive frequency-domain modulation. Finally, a progressive multiscale reconstruction strategy integrates the modulated features to generate high-resolution MS (HRMS) images. Extensive experiments on four satellite datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework under both reduced-resolution (RR) and full-resolution (FR) evaluation protocols, achieving competitive or superior performance compared with representative state-of-the-art methods.
item.authors: Xuebin Li;Qiang Liu;Lingling Yang;Yu Zhang;Guangwei Zhao;Gangqiang Li;Jinfeng Gao;

item.title: Spatial–Frequency Collaborative Decoupling and Adaptive Gating Network for High-Resolution Remote Sensing Image Semantic Segmentation
item.description: Semantic segmentation of high-resolution remote sensing images faces challenges due to intraclass heterogeneity and interclass spectral similarity. Traditional single-domain methods struggle to balance computational efficiency, high-frequency details, and a global receptive field. To address this, we propose the spatial–frequency collaborative decoupling and adaptive gating network (DSFANet). The model employs a parallel convolutional neural network (CNN)–Transformer architecture: in the spatial domain, a lightweight large kernel attention (LightLKA) module captures local high-frequency boundaries; in the frequency domain, a 2-D fast Fourier transform (FFT)-based global filter establishes long-range topological dependencies with an ${O}({Nlog}{N})$ complexity. In addition, a scene context-aware gating (SCAG) module aggregates global channel-wise statistics to produce two scalar gating weights for fusing the spatial and frequency representations, and a linear-complexity attention fusion block (AFB) bridges the semantic gap between deep and shallow layers. Experiments on four heterogeneous datasets [Vaihingen, Potsdam, LoveDA, and Gaofen Image Dataset (GID)] show that DSFANet achieves an optimal balance between accuracy and computational cost. Furthermore, interpretability analysis using Grad-class activation mapping (CAM) and t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) confirms that this dual-domain architecture effectively handles local occlusions, reduces semantic aliasing, and improves interclass separability. Overall, this work provides an efficient, reliable, and interpretable method for large-scale, fine-grained land use mapping. The code can be obtained here: https://github.com/LijianXie/DSFA-Net
item.authors: Lijian Xie;Bohua Zhao;Aihua Shen;Zhiguo Li;Xin Zhao;Jinsong Deng;

item.title: A Deformation Compensated Offset Tracking for the High-Velocity Glaciers at Greenland Ice Sheet
item.description: Offset tracking (OT) is a primary method for monitoring glacier motion in high-velocity regions, where displacement is typically estimated by template matching in the frequency domain. However, this method relies on the rigid-body shift assumption of the image template and neglects internal deformation within the template, which may reduce coherence and introduce errors in displacement estimation. Here, we propose a deformation compensation method to eliminate the effects of internal deformation within the template. First, a preset deformation field is formed based on a long-term average flow velocity field and the synthetic aperture radar (SAR) observation geometry. Then the pre-event image is shifted pixelwise according to the preset deformation field to establish a simulated postevent image. Afterward, the residual deformation is obtained by performing the OT method between the simulated postevent image and the real postevent image. The final deformation field is the sum of the preset deformation field and the residual. We selected four glaciers in Greenland and applied the proposed method to Sentinel-1 SAR images. The obtained velocity fields were compared with published velocity products and those derived from the traditional OT method. In the top 10% high-velocity regions, compared with the traditional OT method, the proposed method achieves average improvements of 103.84% in spatial coverage and 1.96 in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR); compared with the published velocity products, the spatial coverage improvement averages 92.44%. The results demonstrate that the proposed deformation-compensated OT method effectively reduces monitoring failures in high-velocity glacier regions and significantly improves the coverage of velocity fields, especially in high-velocity areas. This research can be further applied to both polar and alpine regions for glacier dynamic studies.
item.authors: Ziyin Yao;Gang Li;Yanting Mao;Zhuoqi Chen;Yu Li;Xiao Cheng;

item.title: B-Mamba: Burn Severity Mapping From Large-Scale Landsat Imagery Using a Mamba-Based Siamese Network
item.description: Operational burn severity mapping remains largely dependent on spectral index-based approaches that require manual threshold selection and expert interpretation, limiting scalability and consistency across events. Deep learning methods have improved change detection accuracy, but most have been developed for very high-resolution datasets, reducing their transferability to medium-resolution, globally available sensors, such as Landsat. To address this gap of automating the operational burn severity mapping with deep learning using Landsat images, we propose burn severity Mamba (B-Mamba), a Siamese Mamba-based network that exploits the linear-complexity, long-range dependency modeling of state-space architectures while explicitly capturing pre to postfire changes through dual-branch feature extraction, hierarchical change fusion, and a progressive reconstruction decoder. On the large-scale Landsat-BSA benchmark dataset, B-Mamba achieves the state-of-the-art performance, reaching a mean intersection-over-union (mIoU) of 79.31% and an overall accuracy (OA) of 95.70%, outperforming leading convolutional, transformer-based, and existing Mamba-based change detection models by 3.71%–14.48% points in mIoU. Ablation experiments confirm the importance of the learnable patch-expanding decoder, change fusion, and the proposed composite loss function for accurate severity delineation. Additional evaluations on independent wildfire events within and outside the contiguous United States (Alaska and Hawaii), including evaluations on Sentinel-2 imagery, demonstrate the robustness and generalization of the approach. These results indicate that Mamba-based state-space architectures provide a scalable, effective pathway toward operational, large-area burn severity mapping from medium-resolution satellite imagery.
item.authors: S. M. Sohel Rana;Taejun Sung;Rogelio Ruzcko Tobias;Jungho Im;Yoojin Kang;Jaese Lee;

item.title: BFDMCA: A Novel Approach for Classification of GPR Images With SHAP Explanations
item.description: Accurate classification of clutter-free images is crucial for precise analysis in ground penetrating radar (GPR) imaging. However, significant challenges arise due to limited annotated datasets and the demand for efficient models capable of handling complex subsurface data. Existing methods often struggle to differentiate subtle features critical for accurate classification, where fine details are essential. To address these challenges, the proposed model employs an optimized architecture combined with a multiscale attention mechanism, achieving improved classification accuracy and robustness in GPR imaging. The approach begins with the collection of synthetic and experimental GPR images, followed by data augmentation through conditional generative adversarial networks (CGANs), which enrich data diversity and volume, strengthening classification accuracy. For classification, the model employs the bidirectional focal Tversky dynamic multiscale convolutional neural network based on AlexNet (BFDMCA), which integrates multiscale convolutional feature extraction with bidirectional long–short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) and attention mechanisms to capture complementary spatial and sequential information from GPR images. Explainability is supported by Shapley additive explanation (SHAP), which provides insights into critical features and regions, ensuring model transparency and reliability. A lightweight web-based application is also implemented to facilitate real-time visualization of predictions, supporting practical use of the proposed framework.
item.authors: Buddepu Santhosh Kumar;Swarna Laxmi Panda;Satyakam Baraha;Ajit Kumar Sahoo;Subrata Maiti;

item.title: Multimodal Remote Sensing Image Classification via Hierarchical Frequency-Enhanced Mamba Fusion Network
item.description: The hyperspectral image (HSI) and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) data provide complementary characteristics that improve the performance of remote sensing image classification. However, the existing multimodal fusion methods still struggle against two critical challenges. First, most cross-modal fusion strategies adopt overly simplistic feature interaction designs, which prevents them from fully exploiting the complementary information between the two modalities. Second, although the Mamba architecture efficiently models long-range dependencies, its inherent tendency toward excessive smoothing limits its ability to capture high-frequency details. To address these challenges, we propose a hierarchical frequency-enhanced Mamba fusion network (HFMNet) for multimodal remote sensing image classification, which enhances global representation capability by integrating state-space modeling with frequency-enhanced analysis. Specifically, the Fourier transform is embedded into the spatial Mamba modules to compensate for their limited sensitivity to high-frequency variations, thereby enhancing the representation of fine-grained spatial details while maintaining efficient long-range dependency modeling. Furthermore, a multilevel dual-attention-guided fusion (ML-DAGF) module is developed to explicitly integrate multimodal features along both spatial and channel dimensions. This design facilitates the alignment and complementary exploitation of heterogeneous information. The level-specific fused representations are then progressively aggregated in a multilevel manner to strengthen multilevel feature consistency and improve classification reliability. Under a challenging few-shot learning scenario (only 20 training samples per class), the comprehensive experiments on Houston2013, MUUFL, and Trento show that our method obtains overall accuracy (OA) values of 95.45%, 86.08%, and 99.35%, respectively. This demonstrates its robust feature extraction capabilities under sparse supervision, and it performs favorably against the state-of-the-art approaches.
item.authors: Ping Li;Qiya Song;Jianle Peng;Linhui Ma;Renwei Dian;Tao Yang;

item.title: Spatially Adaptive Multifrequency Graph Representation and Evolution for Hyperspectral Image Clustering
item.description: Hyperspectral image clustering aims to discover land-cover category structures in an unsupervised manner. Graph-based methods have shown strong potential for this task by modeling spatial topological relationships and non-Euclidean correlations among samples. However, existing graph-based clustering methods often rely on smooth propagation or introduce frequency responses through graph operators and globally shared weights, which may be insufficient to capture the spatially varying frequency demands of hyperspectral scenes. In particular, homogeneous regions usually require low-frequency consistency enhancement, whereas boundaries, mixed pixels, and fine-grained structures demand stronger high-frequency discrimination. To address this issue, we propose a spatially adaptive multifrequency graph representation and evolution (SAMFGE) framework for hyperspectral image clustering. Specifically, we design a collaborative multifrequency representation module to capture low-frequency homogeneity and high-frequency heterogeneity. A node- and channel-aware frequency coordination (NCAFC) mechanism is then introduced to adaptively assign frequency preferences according to local structural properties and discriminative spectral–spatial responses. Furthermore, the learned multifrequency cues are exploited as interpretable evidence to guide graph evolution, enabling representation learning and topology refinement to co-evolve in a frequency-aware manner. Experimental results on multiple public hyperspectral datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
item.authors: Pan Gao;Huilang Xu;Kaiyu Lin;Guang-Yong Chen;Min Gan;C. L. Philip Chen;

item.title: H2SuperEllipse: Superellipse Representation for Oriented Object Detection With Horizontal Box Supervision
item.description: Oriented object detection is important for aerial image interpretation, where objects often appear with arbitrary orientations and diverse shapes. However, obtaining supervision, such as pixel-wise masks or rotated bounding boxes (RBoxes), is costly, motivating horizontal box (HBox)-supervised methods, such as H2RBox-v2. While using HBoxes reduces annotation costs, the assumption that an HBox is the external circumscribed box of an inferred RBox may not hold for round or near-round objects, and rectangular RBoxes can include substantial background for nonrectangular targets. This article presents H2SuperEllipse, a contour-guided HBox-supervised detector that extends the five-parameter RBox to a six-parameter superellipse representation $(x_{c},y_{c},w,h,\theta,n)$ for both square-like and round-like objects. The shape exponent $n$ describes instance-level object extent, while omitting $n$ naturally recovers the standard RBox output. Without mask or shape-parameter annotations, edge refinement (ER) extracts edge cues inside HBoxes, contour-guided superellipse pseudo-labeling (CGSP) estimates pseudo-labels for $n$ , and superellipse circumscribed loss supervises the predicted superellipse from HBox annotations. On DOTA-v1.0, H2SuperEllipse achieves 73.58% AP50, exceeding manual-prior and prior-free H2RBox-v2 by 1.42 and 4.06 points. On a matched iSAID subset, the superellipses improve C-IoU from 73.90% to 75.20% and reduce background inclusion from 19.60% to 9.00% relative to the RBoxes from the same predictions. These results suggest that the proposed superellipse representation offers a new balance between annotation efficiency and geometric accuracy.
item.authors: Mengqing Tang;Yi Yu;Feipeng Da;Shaoyan Gai;

item.title: A Cross-Gating PINN With Physics-Guided Multiscale Spatial Phase for Wavefield Simulation
item.description: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), as mesh-free solvers for partial differential equations (PDEs), often encounter the high-frequency fitting predicament caused by spectral bias and local wavefront distortion when solving frequency-domain wave equations (Helmholtz equations). Moreover, traditional data-driven random weight initialization easily introduces unphysical artifacts and computational redundancy in feature space. To address these issues, this article proposes a novel neural wavefield solver, CG-MSP-PINN, based on physical priors of multiscale spatial phase and cross-gating mechanisms. First, the physical dispersion relation of the wave equation is explicitly mapped onto Cartesian wave vectors, constructing a feature distribution in wavenumber space with strict physical boundaries to suppress nonphysical noise. Second, a dual-band physical feature dictionary is designed: global broadband absolute phase is used to fit the macroscopic smooth background, while local single-frequency relative phase captures abrupt variations in the target dominant frequency band. Furthermore, a dual-branch cross-gating fusion architecture is introduced, enabling synergistic representation through bidirectional nonlinear modulation between implicit wavefield characterization via sinusoidal representation networks (SIRENs) and explicit multiscale physical dictionaries. Numerical experiments across frequency bands using Simple and Marmousi models demonstrate that CG-MSP-PINN effectively mitigates scale aliasing problems. Compared to pure SIREN architectures, this method achieves higher wavefield reconstruction accuracy while reducing dependence on spatial collocation density and training duration. This study provides a deep learning solution that takes into account both physical constraints and computational efficiency for seismic exploration and full waveform inversion.
item.authors: Daoxuan Li;Zhen’an Yao;Hongxing Li;Wanling Chen;Xiangteng Wang;

item.title: EIRSAM: Enhancing Segment Anything for Domain-Generalized Infrared Small-Target Detection
item.description: Infrared small-target detection is essential for security monitoring, maritime rescue, and public safety, yet its performance often degrades severely under domain shifts caused by varying imaging conditions and sensor characteristics. Existing domain generalization (DG) methods alleviate this issue to some extent, but cross-domain detection remains challenging when targets exhibit weak contrast and occupy only a few pixels. This motivates us to investigate whether large-scale pretrained visual priors, combined with infrared-specific feature learning, can improve performance on unseen domains. To this end, we propose EIRSAM, a segment anything model (SAM)-based adaptation network for domain-generalized infrared small-target detection. Built upon a frozen SAM backbone, EIRSAM introduces a dual-branch encoder–decoder architecture to jointly exploit the transferable visual priors of the foundation model and the fine-grained structural cues of infrared imagery. A feature-gated fusion module (FGFM) is designed to balance domain-general semantic representations and infrared-specific local structures, while a hierarchical mask decoder (HMD) equipped with mask-guided category self-attention (MGCSA) and bidirectional cross-mask interaction is developed to suppress background interference and refine target-focused prediction. In addition, a hierarchical loss strategy is introduced to stabilize coarse-to-fine optimization and improve prediction consistency under cross-domain conditions. Extensive experiments on multiple infrared small-target benchmarks demonstrate that EIRSAM consistently improves detection accuracy and false alarm suppression on unseen domains, validating its effectiveness for robust cross-domain infrared small-target detection.
item.authors: Weijian Chi;Jiahang Liu;Yue Ni;Xifu Sun;Hui Zhang;

item.title: Conditional Cramér–Rao Bound Analysis of Medium-Frequency Radar Horizontal Wind Retrieval and Comparison With Full Correlation Analysis
item.description: Full correlation analysis (FCA) is widely used for horizontal wind retrieval with medium-frequency (MF) radar. This study derives an analytical Fisher-information matrix (FIM) and Cramér–Rao bound (CRB) from the adopted full-echo likelihood under a fixed and known scattering realization. Under the corresponding regularity and unbiasedness conditions, the CRB provides a conditional covariance lower bound that complements existing variance and precision analyses of specified FCA/spaced-antenna estimators. A conditional full-signal maximum-likelihood estimator provides numerical evidence of high-signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) tightness. Conventional FCA is evaluated relative to this benchmark, although the resulting gap cannot be attributed solely to processing loss because the benchmark assumes additional scattering-realization knowledge. The local full-signal correction analysis quantifies the reference-wind accuracy required to remain near the conditional bound. In the investigated configuration, the mismatch allowed by a 10%-near-CRB criterion decreases from approximately 0.424 m/s at 0 dB to 0.105 m/s at 30 dB. An FCA-initialized correction improves the retrieval error but remains above this conditional benchmark. Measured echoes provide qualitative checks of selected observable characteristics and illustrate externally assisted correction; they do not independently validate the conditional CRB. The results establish a model-specific information benchmark and clarify the reference-accuracy requirements for approaching it under prescribed scattering knowledge.
item.authors: Yang Zhang;Li-Ming Wang;Na Li;

item.title: Language-Guided Manifold Learning for Cross-Domain Remote Sensing Object Detection
item.description: Cross-domain remote sensing object detection under the single-domain generalized object detection (SDGOD) setting is crucial for deploying detectors in unseen target domains. Existing methods typically perform feature fusion and matching in Euclidean space with a fixed inner-product metric, which may overlook feature geometry and cause biased similarity estimation under domain shift. Even when structured geometry is modeled, maintaining manifold feasibility across layers remains challenging. Moreover, instance-level text in detection and localization scenarios is often too short and sparse to provide reliable cross-domain semantic anchors. To address the above issues, we propose a language-guided manifold learning network (LMLNet), a vision–language model (VLM) framework for cross-domain generalizable object detection in remote sensing. First, we propose affine-invariant Riemannian metric (AIRM) calibrated cross-attention (AccA), which models feature geometry with an AIRM-induced metric to reduce the similarity-estimation bias caused by fixed inner-product matching under cross-domain shifts. Second, we propose a geometry-preserving bilinear mapping (GPB) with Stiefel-constrained optimization to preserve geometric constraints during network forward propagation. Finally, we propose a text denoising key–value (TDKV) mechanism, which introduces textual attribute noise to enhance the robustness of text guidance under weak instance-level semantics. Experiments on M3VL and DIOR2HRRSD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and cross-dataset generalizability of LMLNet. The project resources are available at https://github.com/softwarePupil/LMLNet
item.authors: Haoxiang Chen;Wei Zhao;Xiping Shang;Rufei Zhang;Nannan Li;Dongjin Li;

item.title: BCSCENet: Background Clutter Suppression and Contrast Enhancement Network for Infrared Small Target Detection
item.description: Infrared small target detection (IRSTD) aims to accurately segment target regions from complex infrared scenes. Since small targets usually occupy only a few pixels and suffer from weak local contrast, blurred boundary structures, and strong background clutter interference, existing methods are still prone to missed detections and false alarms. Although deep learning methods have improved small-target representation through multiscale feature fusion, attention mechanisms, and context modeling, small-target features may still be overwhelmed or falsely enhanced by background responses during feature extraction and decoding in complex backgrounds. To address these challenges, we propose a background clutter suppression and contrast enhancement network (BCSCENet). The network is based on a U-shaped encoder–decoder structure and enhances the ability to model complex scenes in terms of three aspects, including smooth background trends, structured background interference, and local foreground–background differences. Specifically, the differentiable planar background suppression (DPBS) module suppresses low-frequency responses caused by continuous background regions by estimating local planar background trends. The structure tensor anisotropy gate (STAG) module models anisotropic structures using local gradient directional consistency, thereby weakening structured clutter interference such as edges and stripes. The local contrast residual enhancement (LCRE) module highlights the response differences between small targets and their neighboring background through local background estimation and positive residual constraint. Experimental results show that BCSCENet outperforms several existing IRSTD methods on two public datasets, IRSTD-1K and NUAA-SIRST. It effectively reduces background false responses, improves small-target region prediction, and maintains low computational cost. These results indicate that combining background clutter suppression with small-target contrast enhancement helps improve the robustness and detection performance of IRSTD in complex infrared scenes.
item.authors: Qian Sun;Song Ming;Zhenshu Zhong;Li Liu;

item.title: Four-Component Scattering Power Decomposition of Polarimetric GPR Data for Enhanced Subsurface Linear Target Identification
item.description: Ground-penetrating radar (GPR) is widely used for subsurface detection and evaluation. Yet, distinguishing different buried objects from radargrams remains challenging. Polarimetric GPR (Pol-GPR) provides richer target scattering information and helps solve this challenge, but existing decomposition methods fail to adequately delineate the dipole-like scattering behavior associated with linear structures such as rebars, pipes, and cracks. To address this limitation, this article proposes a four-component power decomposition tailored for both fully polarimetric and dual-polarimetric GPR systems. Within Dey’s model-free framework, the method uses $\Re (T_{12})$ to define a dipole-like parameter and the corresponding power component. Analytical solutions for an infinitely long PEC cylinder show that $\Re (T_{12})$ reflects the difference between the parallel- and perpendicular-polarization responses and varies with target orientation. Laboratory experiments on four typical targets—a metallic sphere, a dihedral, a thin dipole target, and a reinforcing bar (rebar)—demonstrate that the proposed method effectively highlights their dominant scattering mechanisms. Field applications to reinforced concrete inspection and ice-crack detection illustrate the practical applicability of the proposed approach in identifying linear targets with dipole-like responses under realistic conditions. These results indicate that the proposed four-component decomposition algorithm and data processing workflow exhibit promising potential for engineering applications using Pol-GPR.
item.authors: Bin Zhang;Hai Liu;Pei Wu;Zhenjun Zhu;Xu Meng;Xiaoyu Zhang;

item.title: ST-AVIT: A Semantic Prior-Guided and Thermal Structure-Constrained Model for Aerial Visible-to-Infrared Image Translation
item.description: Visible-to-infrared (V2IR) image translation offers a practical approach to alleviating the high acquisition cost of infrared data and the scarcity of paired cross-modal samples. However, insufficient consideration of land-cover-dependent infrared responses can cause inaccurate target intensities, blurred boundaries, and response mixing across heterogeneous regions. To address these problems, we propose ST-AVIT, a semantic prior-guided and thermal structure-constrained model for aerial V2IR image translation. The model concatenates dataset-adaptive semantic maps with visible images along the channel dimension, providing explicit spatial and category-boundary information to distinguish adjacent land-cover regions. A physics-inspired temperature–emissivity–semantic (TeS) radiation network is pretrained on real infrared images using the corresponding visible-image-derived semantic label maps and frozen as a teacher. It constrains feature consistency between generated and reference infrared images, providing additional supervision for regional infrared response modeling without requiring the teacher during inference. Experiments on the aerial V2IR Image Dataset (AVIID)-3 dataset, together with supplementary validation on the ground-level multi-scenario multi-modality dataset (M3FD) dataset, show that ST-AVIT outperforms eight competing adversarial and diffusion-based methods across all four evaluated metrics. These results indicate improvements in pixel-level reconstruction, structural similarity, perceptual quality, and distributional agreement with real infrared imagery on both datasets. Qualitative comparisons show better preservation of object–background contrast, local boundaries, small targets, and regional infrared intensity patterns. Image-level and category-level ablation studies demonstrate that semantic input conditioning and TeS regularization jointly improve structural fidelity and regional infrared response modeling.
item.authors: Yandong Wang;Xingyun Liu;Lei Dai;Xiaoqing Mei;Xuedong Yao;Mingxuan Dou;Ruipeng Li;Dongyang Wang;

item.title: RiRUFold: Rethinking Sparse Reweighted Mask Tensor Unfolding Network for Infrared Small-Target Detection
item.description: Infrared small-target detection (ISTD) remains a challenging task because small targets usually occupy only a few pixels and lack clear texture or shape information, while complex infrared backgrounds often contain strong edges, cloud clutter, and target-like interference. Existing deep unfolding methods exploit low-rank and sparse priors to provide target-background separation, but their performance is often limited by fixed low rank and sparse assumptions and hand-crafted parameters. To address these issues, this article proposes a sparse reweighted mask tensor unfolding network, termed RiRUFold, for ISTD. In particular, unlike traditional low-rank and sparse decomposition methods that rely on fixed regularization weights, we design RiRUFold from the perspective of sparse reweighted mask tensor (SRMT) modeling. First, we formulate ISTD as an SRMT-constrained optimization problem, where a learnable SRMT is introduced to dynamically assign regularization. Then, we unfold this iterative optimization into a stagewise deep network architecture, where each stage integrates four modules tailored for SRMT modeling. A low-rank separation module that efficiently estimates structured backgrounds without explicit SVD computation. The sparse target extraction module leverages the reweighted mask to robustly extract dim small targets. Furthermore, extensive experiments on public ISTD datasets demonstrate that RiRUFold outperforms representative model-driven and deep-learning-based methods in terms of detection accuracy and robustness under low signal-to-noise ratios and complex backgrounds.
item.authors: Guoxia Xu;Yao Zhang;Kang Chen;Lizhen Deng;Hu Zhu;

item.title: A Superresolution Reconstruction Network With Feature-Similarity-Difference-Based Fusion
item.description: Multiframe superresolution (MFSR) reconstruction algorithms have been extensively studied, where the fusion stage plays a crucial role in preserving image details and enhancing reconstruction quality. Although existing weighted fusion methods have achieved certain improvements in reconstruction performance, they still suffer from insufficient exploitation of interframe information and loss of detail. To address this issue, we propose a superresolution (SR) fusion approach based on differences in feature similarity. In particular, the similarity between each frame and the reference frame is first computed, and the differences among these similarities are then leveraged to extract complementary interframe information. Pixelwise fusion weights are further employed to optimize the information fusion process. In addition, the fusion stage incorporates a multiscale attention residual module, which strengthens feature representation through hierarchical information aggregation. Moreover, to mitigate the impact of distribution discrepancies between artificially degraded training data and real-world remote sensing data, we employ a domain-adaptive image translation network to preprocess artificially degraded training samples. Extensive experiments are conducted on the DIOR and AID remote sensing datasets, as well as the real Jilin-1 satellite video dataset. Results demonstrate that in the $\times 4$ SR task, our method achieves peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index measure (SSIM) values of 31.07 dB and 0.8268 on the AID dataset, surpassing the HiRN method by 1.02 dB and 0.0718, respectively. On the real-world Jilin-1 video dataset, the proposed method achieves a Blind/Referenceless Image Spatial Quality Evaluator (BRISQUE) score of 46.898, which is 3.004 lower than that of the SA method, indicating favorable no-reference perceptual quality in real remote sensing video scenarios.

item.title: SX-FNO: A Spectral Cross-Gating Fourier Neural Operator for Forward Surrogate Modeling of GPR B-Scans
item.description: Repeated ground-penetrating radar (GPR) simulation with finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) solvers remains computationally demanding for heterogeneous media. This study presents SX-FNO, a spectral cross-gating Fourier neural operator for configuration-specific GPR B-scan surrogate modeling. Separate encoders preserve the distinct representations of relative permittivity and electrical conductivity, while Fourier-domain cross-gating models their interaction before global operator learning. A structure-regularized objective further constrains wavefront morphology and localized scattering features. Experiments on heterogeneous models generated with gprMax show that SX-FNO improves reconstruction over standard U-Net and FNO baselines, reproduces trace-level waveform characteristics in the conditioned domain, and substantially reduces inference cost relative to FDTD. The structural regularizer also suppresses unsupported local curvature, complementing conventional point-wise metrics. These results support SX-FNO as an efficient surrogate for repeated generation of conditioned GPR B-scans under a fixed acquisition configuration.
item.authors: Wenqiang Ding;Changying Ma;Hongxing Li;Wenwu Tang;Xintong Dong;Bingbing Chen;

item.title: Semi-Supervised-Learning-Based Wavelet and Seismic Data Adaptive High-Resolution Reconstruction
item.description: Enhancing seismic resolution is crucial for detecting thin geological layers. Traditional physics-driven methods are generalizable but rely heavily on physical approximations, accurate wavelet estimation, and stationary assumptions. Data-driven approaches, such as deep learning (DL), offer model-independent mappings from low-resolution to high-resolution seismic data but require large well-logging datasets and lack physical interpretability. To overcome these limitations, we propose a semi-supervised learning framework that jointly integrates seismic data, well-log data, and physical models. Our approach introduces an inverse network to map low-resolution seismic data to broadband reflection coefficients. A key innovation is a forward network with two adaptive submodules: one adaptively corrects the initial source wavelet, and the other simulates nonstationary seismic data, ensuring a physically consistent data match. The inverted reflection coefficients are then convolved with a broadband wavelet to produce a stable, high-resolution reconstruction. Tests on synthetic and field data demonstrate that our method achieves improved resolution and reliable performance, even with limited well-log labels.
